column3: The deployed API is reachable and its docs are live. Checked by opening the URLs in the README.
column6: The API answers at a public HTTPS URL and /swagger-ui.html loads with annotated endpoints.
column9: Either the API is unreachable or Swagger is not served on the deployment.
column12: Nothing is deployed, or the URLs in the README do not resolve.

column3: The contract-first work, in the repository, in /docs.
column6: openapi.yaml, ER diagram, auth sequence diagram, error model and two ADRs are all committed, and the implementation matches the contract.
column9: Most artifacts are present but one is missing or the implementation has drifted from the contract.
column12: Only the ER diagram or only a generated spec; no hand written contract.
column15: No design artifacts in the repository.

column3: Verified from the repository and from the Actions tab.
column6: Coverage floor enforced by the build, REST Assured integration tests on Testcontainers covering happy and error paths, Android tests present, and CI green on the default branch.
column9: Tests exist and CI runs, but the coverage gate is missing or the error paths are not covered.
column15: No meaningful tests, or CI is red or absent.

column3: Multi stage build, compose for local development, and an image built by CI.
column6: Multi stage Dockerfile and .dockerignore, docker-compose.yml brings the stack up, CI builds the image and publishes to GHCR, and no secrets are baked in.
column9: The image builds but one of compose, the CI build or the registry publish is missing.
column12: No working Dockerfile, or credentials committed to the repo or the image.

column3: detekt, with a committed ruleset, wired so violations fail the build.
column6: detekt configured in both repos with a committed ruleset, failing the build, and running in CI.
column9: detekt is configured but runs on defaults with no committed config, or does not fail the build.
column12: No static analysis on the default branch.

column3: The client as an artifact, not a recording.
column6: A debug APK is attached to a GitHub release, screenshots of all four screens are committed, and the app talks to the live API.
column9: The app is in the repo but there is no release artifact, or screens are missing.

column3: Could a stranger clone this and run it?
column6: README in each repo with setup, Docker commands, the live URL and the Swagger link, plus KDoc or Javadoc on public classes and methods.
column9: The README exists but a new person would get stuck, or documentation comments are largely absent.
